facts.title: Dartmouth Center for Social Impact
facts.summary: Dartmouth's center for community-driven experiential learning, which prepares students to address pressing societal problems.
facts.hook: offers community-driven experiential learning aimed at pressing societal problems
facts.quote: The Dartmouth Center for Social Impact educates students to be transformative leaders for the common good. Through community-driven experiential learning, our students cultivate their skills, scholarship, and passion to develop high-impact approaches to the most pressing societal problems.
facts.sourceTitle: Mission and Vision | Students | Social Impact
facts.commonnessReason: The college's main service and community engagement center.

facts.title: Nelson A. Rockefeller Center for Public Policy and the Social Sciences
facts.summary: Dartmouth's public policy center, which offers policy courses, a public policy minor, research opportunities, skills training, and visits from scholars and practitioners.
facts.hook: trains students in public policy through courses, policy research, and skills training
facts.quote: The Rockefeller Center educates, trains, and inspires the next generation of public policy leaders, across fields, through multidisciplinary policy and social science-focused education, engagements and public lectures with distinguished visiting scholars and practitioners, policy-oriented research across the social sciences, and skills training.
facts.sourceTitle: Dartmouth College - The Nelson A. Rockefeller Center for Public Policy
facts.commonnessReason: One of Dartmouth's best-known centers and a frequent reference in Why Dartmouth essays.

facts.title: ENGS 14: Technology Entrepreneurship
facts.summary: An introductory course on technology entrepreneurship and the venture ecosystem, designed for undergraduates from all majors.
facts.hook: introduces students from any major to how technology ventures are started, funded, and grown
facts.quote: It is designed for undergraduate students from all majors, including science, engineering, and the humanities who seek to better understand the entrepreneurial mindset as applied to the commercialization of new technologies and its key processes and challenges.

facts.title: ENGS 18: System Dynamics in Policy Design and Analysis
facts.summary: An introduction to system dynamics, a feedback- and simulation-based approach to designing policies, with no prior engineering or computer science experience required.
facts.hook: teaches computer simulation of feedback systems as a tool for designing and analyzing policy
facts.quote: This course introduces systems dynamics, an approach to policy design and analysis based upon feedback principles and computer simulation. ... No prior engineering or computer science experience is necessary.

facts.title: ENGS 21: Introduction to Engineering
facts.summary: The introductory engineering course, in which students work as a team on a complete design project applied to a real problem from initial concept to final recommendations.
facts.hook: puts students on a team design project that takes a real problem from initial concept to final recommendations
facts.quote: The student is introduced to engineering through participation, as a member of a team, in a complete design project. ... Engineering principles of analysis, experimentation, and design are applied to a real problem, from initial concept to final recommendations.
facts.commonnessReason: The required gateway design course for the engineering major, so engineering applicants often mention it.

facts.title: ENGS 28: Embedded Systems
facts.summary: An early-stage engineering course that introduces physical sensors and actuators and how to connect and program them on a microcontroller, aimed partly at students who started with Arduino.
facts.hook: takes students from hobby-level Arduino projects to programming sensors and actuators on a microcontroller
facts.quote: Many students have been exposed to the potential of embedded systems at the hobby or maker level through robotics and the boards such as the popular Arduino and are excited to go farther. ... Engs 28 will introduce you to a variety of physical sensors and actuators, and how to connect them to a microcontroller.

facts.title: ENGS 37: Introduction to Environmental Engineering
facts.summary: A survey of the sources, measurement techniques, and treatment technologies for pollution, covering water pollution, air pollution, solid wastes, and pollutant fate and transport.
facts.hook: introduces how engineers measure and treat water and air pollution, using design examples and case studies
facts.quote: A survey of the sources, measurement techniques, and treatment technologies relating to environmental pollution resulting from the activities of humans. ... Technological and other issues will be addressed relating to water pollution, air pollution, solid wastes, and the fate and transport of pollutants in the environment.

facts.title: ENGS 42: Watershed Hydrology
facts.summary: A course on how water and sediment move through watersheds, including runoff, streamflow, and the transport and fate of contaminants, taught through field and computational methods.
facts.hook: trains students to make field measurements and analyze environmental data on runoff, streamflow, and contaminants
facts.quote: The processes controlling the generation of runoff and streamflow are highlighted and used to explore the transport and fate of sediment and contaminants in watersheds. Throughout the course, ideas and concepts are explored through field and computational methods, with emphasis given to developing observational skills, making field measurements, and doing environmental data analysis.

facts.title: ENGS 43: Environmental Transport and Fate
facts.summary: An introduction to groundwater resources taught through case studies on groundwater budgets, well hydraulics, numerical modeling, contaminant transport, and water quality standards.
facts.hook: uses case studies to teach groundwater modeling, contaminant transport, and water quality standards
facts.quote: This course is an introduction to groundwater and groundwater resources. ... The case studies also provide insight into the complexity of sustainable groundwater resource management through the exploration of the ideas of safe yield, surface-groundwater interactions, and water quality standards.

facts.title: ENGS 45: Sustainable Urban Systems (Berlin)
facts.summary: An engineering course on the technology of urban sustainability, from energy, air quality, and water supply to transportation, decarbonization, and city planning.
facts.hook: examines how cities handle energy, air quality, water, transportation, and decarbonization through an engineering lens
facts.quote: This engineering course addresses the technological aspects of urban sustainability, including energy procurement, energy consumption and green energy, air quality, water supply, use and treatment, building infrastructure, transportation, resource conservation, decarbonization, city planning and the role of automation and information technology in modern sustainable cities.

facts.title: ENGS 8: Understand Energy
facts.summary: A course that builds literacy in energy technologies, from batteries to heat pumps, with field trips, labs, and attention to the policies reshaping the energy landscape.
facts.hook: builds energy literacy through field trips, labs, and discussion of the policies reshaping power demand
facts.quote: This course builds students' literacy around energy technologies (from batteries to heat pumps), impacts, and the undergirding science. Students engage with readings, discussions, and problem sets; experience energy in the real world through field trips and labs; and explore news about the events, shifting policies, and increasing demand for power that are reshaping the energy landscape.

facts.title: ENGS 85.16: Energy and Climate Systems Analysis and Decision Making
facts.summary: A course on decision analysis and systems modeling for energy systems and climate change mitigation, ending in a real-world case study with local or regional stakeholders.
facts.hook: applies decision analysis and energy-climate models to a real case study with local or regional stakeholders
facts.quote: This course introduces the principles of decision analysis and systems modeling, with a focus on energy systems and climate change mitigation applications. ... To bridge theory and practice, students will apply these tools to a real-world case study in partnership with local or regional stakeholders.

facts.title: ENGS 89: Engineering Design Methodology and Project Initiation
facts.summary: The first half of a two-term team design sequence (ENGS 89/90) in which projects come from specifications submitted by industry and other organizations.
facts.hook: has student teams spend two terms on design projects specified by industry and other organizations
facts.quote: Design projects are developed from specifications submitted by industry and other organizations and are pursued over the course of two quarters as a team project, 89/90.
facts.commonnessReason: The engineering capstone sequence, familiar to many engineering applicants.

facts.title: ENVS 21: Transforming the Energy System: Keeping the Lights on While Saving the Planet
facts.summary: A team-taught course on the shift to renewable energy in New England that ends with a discussion of Dartmouth's own energy transition.
facts.hook: studies New England's renewable energy transition and ends by examining Dartmouth's own energy transition
facts.quote: This course will explore how transitioning to renewable energy systems is a necessary leverage point for addressing human-caused climate change, with a specific focus on how energy for electricity and heat is generated and used in New England. ... The course will culminate in a discussion of Dartmouth's own energy transition as well as regional- and national scale solutions

facts.title: ENVS 50: Environmental Problem Analysis and Policy Formulation
facts.summary: A senior course in which student teams develop policy measures for a local environmental problem and present and defend their recommendations publicly.
facts.hook: has student teams craft and publicly defend policy recommendations for a local environmental problem
facts.quote: Students working together in groups will formulate and justify policy measures that they think would be appropriate to deal with a local environmental problem. ... Considerable field work may be involved, and the final examination will consist of a public presentation and defense of student-generated policy recommendations.

facts.title: GEOG 28: Immigration, Race, and Ethnicity
facts.summary: A geography course on 20th-century immigration to the United States, covering citizenship, social mobility, transnationalism, and Latino, Asian, and European immigrant groups.
facts.hook: examines U.S. immigration, citizenship, and the experiences of Latino, Asian, and European groups
facts.quote: This course examines 20th century immigration to the United States and pays special attention to issues of race and ethnicity. ... We feature nativist reactions to immigration and highlight differences within and between Latino, Asian, and European groups throughout the course.

facts.title: GEOG 42: Water Policy and Politics
facts.summary: A course on the political, social, and legal sides of water resource management and how regulatory agencies and the legal sector handle water issues.
facts.hook: shows how the technical side of hydrology plays out in water policy, regulation, and law
facts.quote: This course is designed to provide students with a general background to the issues confronting water resource management. The course covers the political, social and legal aspects confronting effective water policy decision making. One of the goals is to demonstrate that the technical aspects of hydrology occur within a socio-political arena.

facts.title: GEOG 57: Urban Applications of GIS
facts.summary: A geography course on using GIS to solve urban problems in planning and design, public administration, environmental assessment, land use change, and social and political issues.
facts.hook: teaches students to apply GIS to real urban planning, land use, and public administration problems
facts.quote: This course is about how to use GIS technology to solve urban problems. The application problems that will be discussed in the class are from areas including urban planning and design, public administration, business decision-making, environment assessment, land use change, and social and political issues.

facts.title: GEOG 62.01: River Processes and Watershed Science
facts.summary: A course on how watershed processes supply water and sediment to stream channels and how climate change is shifting watershed and river processes.
facts.hook: connects watershed processes and river sediment to the effects of climate change
facts.quote: This course examines the links between watershed scale processes such as weathering, denudation, and mass wasting on the supply of water and sediment to stream channels on both contemporary and geologic timescales and further evaluates the role of climate change on the magnitude and direction of shifts in watershed and fluvial processes.

facts.title: MUS 35: The Jazz Language
facts.summary: A course that teaches instrumentalists and vocalists the core jazz vocabulary by ear, including transcribing phrases in all 12 keys and learning solos as a class.
facts.hook: trains jazz players to learn phrases and solos by ear and transcribe them in all 12 keys
facts.quote: This course will present the essential elements of the "jazz vocabulary" to instrumentalists and vocalists. ... Students will practice learning phrases by ear, which they will then transcribe and write in 12-keys.

facts.title: MUS 45.12: Advanced Studies in Jazz History: A Century of Jazz at Dartmouth
facts.summary: A research course on Dartmouth's own history with jazz and other forms of Black music, using primary sources, interviews, and oral history.
facts.hook: has students document Dartmouth's century of jazz through archival research and oral history
facts.quote: This term we will be turning our gaze inward, exploring Dartmouth's own history with jazz and other forms of Black music over the past century. Through a combination of primary source research, interviews and oral history, and creative storytelling and writing, the goal of this course is to generate lasting, honest, insightful, and engaging documentation of the complicated history of jazz at Dartmouth.

facts.title: SPAN 73.14: Embodying Care: Immigration, Health, and the Medical Humanities
facts.summary: A seminar co-taught with Geisel faculty in which students study immigrant health in U.S. and Latinx contexts and produce bilingual, public-facing work.
facts.hook: has students study immigrant health in Latinx communities and produce bilingual, public-facing work
facts.quote: Through fiction, theatre, visual art, documentary, and community-engaged methods, students examine immigrant health in U.S. and Latinx contexts and produce bilingual, public-facing work that connects analysis to practice.

facts.title: SPAN 9.02: Culture and Conversation: Spanish for Health Equity
facts.summary: A Spanish course for health and medical settings that examines language and intercultural proficiency in health care access and includes a Social Impact Practicum.
facts.hook: builds Spanish for health settings and examines how language shapes access to care, with a community practicum
facts.quote: The goal is to expand foundational communication skills so that students can use Spanish in academic and professional settings in health and medical fields, and so that they can reflect critically on the role of linguistic and intercultural proficiency in health care access (particularly in the United States). ... it includes a Social Impact Practicum in collaboration with the Center for Social Impact.

facts.title: Engineering Sciences Major Modified with Environmental Sciences
facts.summary: A modified Engineering Sciences major that combines engineering courses with environmental science courses drawn from biology, chemistry, ecology, and earth sciences.
facts.hook: lets an engineering major build in environmental science courses from biology, chemistry, and earth sciences
facts.quote: Modified Major with Environmental Sciences: Students interested in engineering and environmental science may elect an engineering major modified with environmental science courses. Effective preparation for graduate study or professional activity in the environmental sciences requires an assimilation of material traditionally encountered in biology, chemistry, ecology, and earth sciences, as well as in engineering sciences.

facts.title: Engineering Sciences Major Modified with Public Policy
facts.summary: A modified Engineering Sciences major for students interested in technology and public policy, with policy tracks that include environment, natural resources, health, and science and technology.
facts.hook: pairs an engineering major with public policy coursework, including an environment and public policy track
facts.quote: Modified major with Public Policy: Students interested in technology and public policy may elect an engineering major modified with public policy. ... Possible tracks include: Environment and Public Policy; Health and Public Policy; Natural resources and Public Policy; and Science/technology and Public Policy.

facts.title: Environmental Studies Major and Minors
facts.summary: The Environmental Studies department offers a major plus minors in Environmental Studies (with Sustainability and Sustainable Energy tracks) and Environmental Science.
facts.hook: offers an Environmental Studies major and minors with Sustainability and Sustainable Energy tracks
facts.quote: To meet the needs of our students, we offer a major in Environmental Studies and two minors: Environmental Studies (tracks available in Environmental Studies, Sustainability or Sustainable Energy) and Environmental Science.
facts.commonnessReason: The main environmental major, so environmentally minded applicants often name it.

facts.title: Dartmouth as Living Lab
facts.summary: A sustainability initiative that uses Dartmouth's campus lands and infrastructure as test sites for research, teaching, and pilots of climate and sustainability solutions.
facts.hook: turns campus lands and buildings into test sites for climate and sustainability research and pilots
facts.quote: Embracing a "Campus as Lab" approach allows students, faculty, and staff collaborate to use our campus to generate research, teaching, and creative scholarship on climate change and sustainability. Campus lands, infrastructure, and spaces become dynamic testing grounds where innovative sustainability solutions are piloted in real time.
facts.sourceTitle: DARTMOUTH AS LIVING LAB | Dartmouth Sustainability

facts.title: Environmental Studies Africa Foreign Study Program (Namibia)
facts.summary: An Environmental Studies foreign study program that travels to Namibia to study environmental issues in the context of southern Africa, open to students of all majors.
facts.hook: takes students of any major to Namibia for field-based environmental study in southern Africa
facts.quote: We also offer the Africa Foreign Study Program that travels to Namibia where we explore the themes of environmental studies within the particular environment, culture and history of the southern Africa region. ... The program benefits from having diverse perspectives among the student participants, and all majors are welcome to apply.

facts.title: First Year Research in Engineering Experience (FYREE)
facts.nameOnPage: First Year Research in Engineering Experience
facts.summary: A paid research internship that pairs first-year students and prospective engineering majors with engineering faculty for two terms of lab research.
facts.hook: pairs first-year students with engineering faculty for a paid, two-term research internship in their labs
facts.quote: The First Year Research in Engineering Experience (FYREE) program is a paid research internship that provides early hands-on research experience and mentoring within the engineering sciences for first-year Dartmouth undergraduate students and prospective engineering majors. ... During the program, FYREE students are paired with engineering faculty and take part in active research in their labs.
facts.sourceTitle: First Year Research in Engineering Experience | Dartmouth Engineering

facts.title: Policy Research Shop
facts.summary: A Rockefeller Center program in which students research policy questions requested by New Hampshire and Vermont state, county, and local government officials.
facts.hook: has students research policy questions for New Hampshire and Vermont state and local officials
facts.quote: The Center sponsors the Policy Research Shop, a student-staffed, faculty-mentored research enterprise in which students conduct research at the request of New Hampshire and Vermont state, county, and local government officials.
facts.sourceTitle: Dartmouth College - The Nelson A. Rockefeller Center for Public Policy

facts.title: Social Impact Practicums (SIPs)
facts.summary: Course-based projects that connect Dartmouth classes with needs identified by Upper Valley nonprofits, including human-centered design projects in Thayer's Senior Design Challenge.
facts.hook: connects coursework to projects for Upper Valley nonprofits, including engineering design projects
facts.quote: A Social Impact Practicum (SIP) is a project-based experiential learning opportunity connecting undergraduate courses at Dartmouth with community needs identified by nonprofit organizations throughout the Upper Valley. ... DCSI also collaborates with Thayer's Senior Design Challenge to match human-centered design projects proposed by Upper Valley nonprofits with this two-term senior-level engineering course.
facts.sourceTitle: Social Impact Practicums (SIPs) | Students | Social Impact

facts.title: Undergraduate Research Assistantships at Dartmouth (URAD)
facts.summary: A program that funds undergraduates to work as part-time research assistants with Dartmouth faculty, with a stipend paid at the end of each term of research.
facts.hook: pays undergraduates a stipend to work as part-time research assistants with faculty
facts.quote: Undergraduates experience research first-hand by working with Dartmouth faculty in part-time research assistantships. Students receive a stipend at the end of the completed term of research.
facts.sourceTitle: Undergraduate Research Assistantships at Dartmouth (URAD) | Scholars Programs, Undergraduate Research, and Fellowships at Dartmouth
facts.commonnessReason: A broad research-funding program that many science-minded applicants mention.
